subjects.displayTitle: Heaven and hell: nearness, fulfilment, and mystery
subjects.introduction: Paradise, Bahá’u’lláh writes, means first and foremost the good-pleasure of God, and it is a reality, realised already in this world through love of Him; after death it opens into a vastness that pen and ink cannot describe. Asked where paradise and hell are, He answered that the one is meeting Him and the other is a person’s own self. The Báb adds that each created thing reaches its paradise when it attains the perfection possible to it, and that its failure is its hell. Heaven and hell therefore begin as acceptance and rejection, and continue beyond the grave in conditions no present mind can picture, though the Writings speak of gardens, living waters, chambers of emerald and ruby, and companions who welcome the arriving soul. The Qur’an too sets the pleasure of God above the gardens it promises [1]. Warnings and consolations alike press the same question: what nearness is possible now. The path continues toward the soul and the spirit after death, nearness and remoteness, and the recompense of belief and right action.
subjects.arc: Begin with paradise as divine good-pleasure, explore fulfilment and deprivation, then enter the symbolic promises and consolations of the life beyond.

order.why: Open with a definition that changes the question.
Join present love to life beyond death.
shortened: As to Paradise: It is a reality and there can be no doubt about it, and now in this world it is realized through love of Me and My good-pleasure. Whosoever attaineth unto it God will aid him in this world below, and after death He will enable him to gain admittance into Paradise whose vastness is as that of heaven and earth.

order.why: Explore paradise as the fulfilment of potential.
Develop the flower and human destiny analogy.
shortened: Nothing has been created without a special destiny, for every creature has an innate station of attainment. This flower has been created to mirror forth a harmonious ensemble of color and perfume. Each kingdom of nature holds potentialities and each must be cultivated in order to reach its fulfillment. The divine teachers desire man to be educated that he may attain to the high rank of his own reality, the deprivation of which is the rank of perdition.

order.why: Distinguish present recognition from indescribable future conditions.
shortened: In brief, paradise and hellfire in this outward life have been and shall ever be acceptance and rejection. After the ascension of the spirit to paradises beyond compare, and likewise to hellfire beyond similitude - which are the fruits of the deeds of the one who accepteth and the one who rejecteth - they shall attain thereunto. However, none save God hath comprehended or shall comprehend those stations. For the believer, stations have been created surpassing all that hath been heard of God's wondrous bounties ordained in the paradises of transcendent glory, and likewise for the one who turneth away, beyond what hath been heard of eternal and imperishable torments.

order.why: Keep both this world and the next in view.
shortened: Heaven and hell exist both in this world and in the next world.

And in the next world too, there are countless paradises prepared for the believers and sincere ones, and the spirits of holy souls enjoy all heavenly blessings and divine favors, while the spirits of the deniers and people of error and the adversaries are caught in hell and torment, abased and humiliated.

order.why: Let the direct question sharpen the personal challenge.
shortened: He asked: "Where are Paradise and Hell?" Say: The former is meeting Me and the latter is your own self, O doubting idolater!

order.why: Connect love, recognition and divine good-pleasure.
shortened: Thou admittest whom Thou willest into Thy love and good-pleasure, which is the highest of Thy heavens and Thy paradise, and Thou deniest whom Thou willest from recognizing Thy Proof and His good-pleasure - that is the fire which Thou hast promised to the sinning among Thy servants.

order.why: Explains paradise through spiritual knowledge and perfection.
Read the reported account of moral and spiritual states.
shortened: Hell is the state of mind in which there are evil thoughts and purposes, yielding to the desires of the senses, clinging to material things. In that state man is separated from God, and in his ignorance he suffers.
Salvation - heaven - is the conscious realisation of God in this life, which is gained by love, kindness, and good deeds.

order.why: Concentrate the warning into heedlessness.
Consider disharmony with the divine will.
shortened: A wicked soul is the only thing out of harmony in the universe. As it does not come into the flow of the Divine Will, it is not of the Spirit. This failure of the soul has led man to believe that God will give the wicked soul another opportunity by allowing it to return in another body and atone for its failure. There is no proof of this outside or inside the Holy Book of Scriptures. Whatever is the destiny of the wicked soul in the hereafter, we know that its development rests with the Mercy of God.

order.why: Read the tyrant’s consequences with the fuller source’s rejection of inherited spiritual guilt.
Relate deprivation to wrongful acquisition.
Hear the summons to recognition.
Retain the contrasting destinies of belief and rejection.
shortened: Such as have believed in God and in His signs are indeed the followers of truth and shall abide in the gardens of delight, while those who have disbelieved in God and have rejected that which He hath revealed, these shall be the inmates of the fire wherein they shall remain forever.

order.why: Join the promise to fidelity to the covenant.
shortened: As for those who fulfill God's covenant and purchase not any of the verses for a paltry price -- these are guided by God's Remembrance, the Most High, and these are truly the companions of Paradise in God's Book, and thus hath it been inscribed in the Mother Book. These are they who believe in God and His verses with pure and sincere truth. God shall soon reward them on the Day of Resurrection with a double portion and a goodly final abode, elevated in truth upon truth.

Hath not God promised you a Paradise whose breadth is as the breadth of heaven and earth, prepared for Our servants who believe in the remembrance of God, the Most High, and who are pure in truth and for the sake of truth? Therein shall ye have whatsoever your souls desire, by Our leave -- bounties fresh and delectable, in truth and for the sake of truth.

order.why: Acknowledge the limits of what is presently disclosed.
Enter the Báb’s imagery of two gates and waters.
Read the symbolic stations without inventing a chronological key.
Contemplate the Báb’s imagery of transformed embodiment.
Continue into luminous palaces and remembrance.
Locate sacred imagery within its particular revealed address.
shortened: God hath created for us therein white chambers wherein we were among those who glorify Him, then yellow chambers wherein we were among those who give thanks, then green chambers wherein we were among those who testify to His oneness, then crimson chambers wherein we were among those who magnify Him.

Say: The outer chambers are of emerald which when ye behold them ye are drawn to exclaim: "God beareth witness that there is no God but Him, the Mighty, the Best-Beloved." Then there are inner chambers created of pieces of ruby wherein ye glorify God, then praise Him, and wherein ye profess His unity, then magnify Him.
This is the Mystery in the kingdom of the heavens and earth and whatsoever is between them. None knoweth it save God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Listen to the garden as a place of divine utterance.
shortened: This is the garden of Paradise, wherein arise the anthems of God, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting; wherein ascend the soul-entrancing melodies warbled by the Nightingale of Eternity upon the twigs of the Divine Lote-Tree; wherein abide the Maids of Heaven whom none hath touched save God, the All-Glorious, the Most Holy; and wherein lieth enshrined that which draweth the needy to the shores of the ocean of true wealth and guideth the people to the Word of God.

order.why: Hear the invitation through opened gates.
shortened: This is the Paradise of eternity - We have opened its gates unto all who are in the heavens and on earth. Hasten thereunto, O ye who are sincere, and turn not back upon your heels.

order.why: Let the promised melodies draw the reader inward.
shortened: Enter ye the Garden by God's leave and eat freely of its bounties.
Soon shall its gates be opened and thou shalt hear the melodies of the birds of Paradise from its precincts.

order.why: Develop the images of birds and living water.
shortened: There shalt thou hear the melodies of the birds of eternity upon the branches of the Divine Lote-Tree, and drink the pure water of holiness from the hands of the heavenly maidens.

order.why: Consider the invitation to partake of spiritual bounty.
shortened: Therefore eat of whatsoever fruits of Paradise thou desirest, for they have been ordained for thee from the presence of One mighty and wise. And find solace with the maidens of Paradise in chambers of luminous glory.

order.why: Read the explicit distinction concerning spiritual imagery.
shortened: Mayest thou grow old and reach old age, and each day take a houri in thine arms and dwell in a palace, so that thou mayest partake of the hyacinth of her hair and they of the corner of her eyebrow. Yet not physical houris who possess naught but appetite and desire naught but money, but rather obtain spiritual houris and take delight in the divine gathering, that thou mayest drink of the Kawthar of the spirit and taste of the fruit of light.

order.why: Connect the fruits of paradise with divine knowledge.
shortened: But those who have believed, these are in the mercy of their Lord and are rejoicing in the holy Ridvan, while the maidens of Paradise wait upon them and they delight in the fruits of divine knowledge.

order.why: Retain the abundance of the promised gifts.
Notice the wine that neither intoxicates nor clouds the mind.
Read the imagery of fragrance and heavenly recognition.
shortened: And the Maids of Paradise, and the secluded Maidens of eternity, and the Countenances whom God created from the light of Glory before the creation of earth and heaven, find his fragrance. And upon their brows is inscribed by the golden Pen: "By God! They are the handmaidens of Glory and were created for those who were martyred in the path of this Youth Who sitteth upon the throne of cloud."

order.why: Let the joyful response of the recipients become audible.
shortened: As for the companions of the right hand, their faces beamed with joy, their souls took flight, their hearts were attracted, their lips smiled, their spirits rejoiced, and they said "This indeed is the supreme triumph in the garden of delight!"

order.why: Keep the language of judgment beside promise.
Retain the contrasting images of reckoning.
Read fear and blessedness as movements of supplication.
shortened: Woe unto me, then woe unto me, if on the field of gathering it should be proclaimed: "Seize him and fetter him, then cast him into the blazing fire, then into a chain seventy cubits long thread him!"

Blessed am I, then blessed am I, shouldst Thou admit me into Thy paradise and clothe me in crimson silk through Thy grace, and feed me of fresh meat through Thy bounty, and give me to drink of pure wine from the cup of Thy mercy.

order.why: Turn the contrast toward a plea for mercy.
Consider the transforming power attributed to divine bounty.
shortened: O my Beloved! If Thou wert to give Thy enemies to drink what Thou hast given Thy loved ones to drink, they would all sacrifice themselves in Thy path. But Thou, in Thy hidden wisdom, hast withheld the Kawthar of immortality from the heedless among Thy creatures and ordained it for the sincere ones among Thy chosen ones.

order.why: Let suffering become a prayer for nearness.
shortened: Then do I beseech Thee, O my God, by the sorrow that hath touched me in Thy way, and that hath never departed from me from the beginnings of Thy days, to cause me to ascend unto the Paradise of Thine eternity, and to raise me unto it through Thy loving-kindness; and deprive me not of that which Thou hast ordained therein of the wondrous bounties of Thy oneness and the jewels of the favours of Thy self-subsistence --  that I may be of them that abide therein and that walk in the neighbourhood of its mercy; lest the whisperings of the devils prevent me from loving Thee, from longing for Thee, from cleaving unto Thee, and from being consumed with yearning for Thee. For it is a Paradise created from the elements of Thy power, and wrought from the subtleties of Thy might, in such wise that its sun shineth and is never eclipsed, its moon is bright and is never darkened, its stars fall not, its houses crumble not, its trees change not, its fruits are never altered, its mysteries are not veiled, its breeze is not cut off, its treasures are not exhausted, its light is not quenched, its garment weareth not away, its verses are not abrogated; its clusters hang nigh, its fruits endure, its leaves are everlasting, its delights are perfect.

order.why: Join patience with promised spiritual attainment.
shortened: Thou hast drunk the choice wine of patience from the hand of the favor of thy Lord, the Chosen One, and hast attained unto that which the denizens of the Most Exalted Paradise and the Supreme Heaven have attained.
For them have been ordained exalted stations beneath the pavilions of grandeur, under the shade of the Tree of Grace, in the Supreme Paradise and Most Exalted Heaven.

order.why: Hear the reassurance of remembrance.
Keep the concise promise to those who desire nearness.
shortened: We have ordained stations in Paradise for everyone who hath desired Us.
Beware lest there appear from thee that which would deprive thee of that which hath been ordained for thee.

order.why: Retain the particular assurance to a believing woman.
Carry remembrance into glad tidings.
shortened: Then convey Our remembrance unto those who are with thee and give them the glad-tidings of a holy and inaccessible paradise.

order.why: Approach the unseen station of a departed person with humility.
shortened: Were you to witness the station of Our servant in the highest Paradise, you would beseech God to raise you up unto him. But it hath been veiled from you by a wisdom that none hath comprehended save God, Who perceiveth all vision while no vision perceiveth Him.

order.why: Read consolation addressed to those left behind.
shortened: O ye who remain of the family of the beloved one on earth! Grieve not for him, for he hath ascended unto the Supreme Companion and now dwelleth in the Most Glorious chambers, companioned by the maidens of paradise. He drinketh from the Kawthar of immortality from the hands of youths whom God hath created from the light of glory, whose faces shine as the sun in spheres of crystal white, illumining all who dwell in paradise.

order.why: Contemplate the welcome described at a soul’s ascent.
shortened: At the time of his ascent, the angels and the Spirit received him and brought him into the highest Paradise, his head adorned with the crown of My Most Glorious Name and his temple with the ornament of My Greatest Favor.

order.why: Keep the particular consolation concerning innocent victims.
shortened: And now the angels of Paradise circle round them with chalices of Kawthar and Salsabil.

And they who were slain, having committed no wrong - round them circle the denizens of the highest Paradise at eventide and at dawn, offering up their very souls in their path, while the people of the Concourse of the near ones derive light from their countenances.

order.why: Connect a life of faithful action with the promised welcome.
shortened: But those who have believed in God and acted according to His command - soon shall the angels and the Spirit receive them with chalices of Kawthar and Salsabil, and give them glad tidings of the presence of God, and usher them into the station wherein shineth the light of the face of your Lord, the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

order.why: Let the ocean image widen the sense of belonging.
Pray for the departed in the language of mercy.
Extend the prayer to companionship and generosity.
Close the linked readings with forgiveness and welcome.
Retain the supplied culmination in purification and divine good-pleasure.

questions: How does defining paradise through divine good-pleasure change the way you imagine a fulfilled life?
What can the garden, water, light, and companionship images communicate that a literal description might miss?
How do the passages hold together spiritual conditions experienced now and an afterlife beyond present comprehension?
What does the Qur’anic comparison add to the relationship between the gifts of paradise and the Giver?
How can warnings about deprivation and injustice deepen responsibility without becoming judgments about another person’s ultimate destiny?
Which connected subject could help you explore the relation between consolation for grief and transformation in this life?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 9:72 · Paradise and divine pleasure
references.note: Read the promise to believing women and men in Mustafa Khattab’s translation: gardens and enduring homes are followed by the greater blessing of divine pleasure. Compare the relationship between these gifts and God’s good-pleasure with the opening passages. The comparison invites reflection on spiritual fulfilment without assuming that every image of the afterlife receives an identical interpretation in the two traditions.

subjects.displayTitle: Marriage: consent, commitment, and shared life
subjects.introduction: Love, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches, can blend two souls until they speak as one, and marriage is the outward fruit of that blending. Bahá’u’lláh surrounds this union with laws that are strikingly practical: the free choice of the couple, which no one may compel; the consent of living parents, sought with patience so that rancour gives way to harmony; a modest dowry; simplicity in place of display; witnesses, so that no promise can later be denied. Each provision guards something tender. The Qur’an’s picture of spouses as a sign of comfort, compassion and mercy [1] makes a fruitful companion, and the official note to the Kitáb-i-Aqdas shows how an earlier permission, made dependent on an equity no husband can fulfil, becomes in effect a law of monogamy [2]. To study these ordinances is to ask what commitment protects: dignity, affection, the welfare of children not yet born. From here the way opens toward marriage as a path of spiritual growth, toward the prayers a couple offers together, and toward the sober mercy of the law of divorce.
subjects.arc: Begin with affinity and free consent, examine the forms and responsibilities of marriage, and read historical plurality provisions alongside authoritative monogamy clarification.

order.why: Distinguish the couple’s choice from parental consent.
Open with marriage as affinity between souls.
Place the household within a prayer for continuing human life.
shortened: O peerless Lord! In Thine almighty wisdom Thou hast enjoined marriage upon the peoples, that the generations of men may succeed one another in this contingent world, and that ever, so long as the world shall last, they may busy themselves at the Threshold of Thy oneness with servitude and worship, with salutation, adoration and praise.

order.why: Make the rejection of compulsion explicit.
shortened: In the religion of God the consent of both parties is necessary. No one can compel a couple to marry - at most we give permission, we do not interfere more than this. Both parties must consent then the consent of the parents on both sides is necessary. This is obligatory.

order.why: Read patience in seeking parental agreement.
shortened: Deliberation and patience are necessary until her mother giveth her consent and thy father and mother also acquiesce. This is the divine commandment!

order.why: Keep the requirements in their stated relationship.
Read the central provisions with the authoritative clarification in view.
shortened: God hath prescribed matrimony unto you. Beware that ye take not unto yourselves more wives than two. Whoso contenteth himself with a single partner from among the maidservants of God, both he and she shall live in tranquillity.

order.why: Make simplicity a practical expression of purpose.
Connect a modest dowry with comfort and unity.
Specify the lowest amount in the cited answer.
Read the stated upper limit.
Retain the particular answer about permitted amounts.
Place the Bábí provision in its own source context.
Keep the related historical provision distinct.
shortened: God hath fixed the dowry at nineteen mithqals of gold, increasing by one mithqal until it reacheth ninety-five mithqals if the bride be from among the people of the city; and if she be from among the people of the villages, nineteen mithqals of silver, increasing by one mithqal until it reacheth ninety-five mithqals - little do ye comprehend this.

order.why: Read the invitation concerning the joining of two souls.
Consider the particular case of consent, contract and dowry.
shortened: As to what thou didst ask: that a certain man hath, of his own person, asserted unto a certain woman that "thou art my wedded wife," and that he and she recited together the verse of consent, and agreed upon a specified dowry in conformity with the ordinance of the Book; that neither party had anyone appointed by them to conclude the contract with leave and permission; and that no other witnesses were present; yet now the woman denieth it, saying: "Never did such a thing take place; it is a lie." What is the duty, and what the ruling? These matters were laid before the Presence; He said: This marriage contract hath not been concluded according to the ordinance of the Book, for the nuptial formula must be recited and a number of persons must be present, that thereafter none may be able to deny. The recitation of the formula is not an obligation, yet witnesses are necessary.

order.why: Recounts a case concerning dowry and its reduction.
Keep the reference to previously revealed provisions.
Read the parallel statement without merging the sources.
shortened: After the consent of both parties and the consent of the parents, they should gather in a place among the God-fearing and recite this blessed sermon with the utmost joy and fragrance. After the recitation of the sermon, the beloved and his beloved should, in a separate place, recite these two blessed verses that were revealed in the Bayan. [The verses mentioned in the Bayan should be written.] Then the husband should deliver the dowry to his wife, and both parties should sign the document, as well as the witnesses.

order.why: Return to the authority of the revealed text.
Examine the prescribed interval after engagement.
shortened: Now the text of the Book is this: When marriage and the union of husband and wife is decided, meaning this girl is promised to this boy and the union is definite, no more than ninety-five days' delay is permitted for preparation of the trousseau and other matters - the wedding must take place. And the marriage contract is on the night of the wedding, meaning there is no interval between contract and wedding.

order.why: Clarify the public confirmation described in this passage.
Retain the concise statement of the interval.
shortened: O 'Ali Aqa, it is explicitly stated in the Book that when a daughter is betrothed, the wedding cannot be delayed more than ninety-five days.

order.why: Read age and engagement provisions as source law, not a substitute for applicable civil law.
shortened: For according to the binding injunction of the Book, ere entering upon one's fifteenth year marriage is not permitted. Nomination and betrothal too should not take place before the wedding: that is, after the engagement no more than 95 days should pass before the marriage. Likewise the consent of both parties is the first condition; yet consent before maturity is invalid, while the age of maturity is set at fifteen.

order.why: Addresses maturity and the consent of the couple and parents in marriage.
Keep the historical age provision in context.
shortened: The marriage of daughters before entering their fifteenth year is not permitted according to the decisive text, as it causes illness in souls and leads to weakness and lassitude in progeny.

order.why: Retain its devotional and legal setting.
shortened: This servant also entreated and implored at the Holy Threshold of the Self-Subsisting Lord that you may be assisted to carry out the divine ordinances, which are that marriage after the maturity of the wife is at age fifteen and is not permitted before maturity.

order.why: Attend to public registration and effective administration.
Distinguish stated provisions from matters referred for legislation.
Consider the breadth of permission across religious communities.
Read kinship claims as historically situated source statements.
Keep the related argument about distant relationships.
Read the call across racial divisions without adopting its biological generalization.
Retain the reported parallel statement with the same distinction.
Keep the reported medical generalization in its historical context.
Turn to the atmosphere children experience in family life.
Notice the preference for mutual consent and joy.
Examine agreement about travel.
shortened: The limits of travel are set forth and recorded in the Book. It must be undertaken with the consent of both parties, that is, regarding the duration.

order.why: Read the particular maintenance ruling in its source setting.
Distinguish an absent spouse from an established death.
Read how established information changes the waiting question.
shortened: The law of waiting was revealed when the husband's fate was concealed, but after its discovery to act according to what is revealed in God's Book was and is beloved.

order.why: Consider remarriage and the responsibilities of an existing family.
Hear the reported refusal to choose marriage for another person.
Keep the separate exhortation concerning marriage.
Introduce the source’s account of gradual change in marriage law.
Read the related historical explanation with its stated condition.
Keep the reported claims about Christian history attributed.
Distinguish earlier personal circumstances from later legislation.
Read the condition of equitable treatment.
Preserve the apparently permissive wording before the clarifications.
Retain the particular letter rather than harmonizing it silently.
Read the restrictions stated in this response.
Keep the brief prohibition and its source omission visible.
Follow the argument from an impossible condition to monogamy.
End the linked sources with the explicit interpretation.
shortened: As for the matter of plural marriage, the Most Great Name enacted it only for a hidden wisdom and divine mystery.

Know that God's law does not permit plural marriage, for it explicitly states contentment with one wife and makes a second wife conditional upon justice and fairness between them in all ranks and conditions. But justice and fairness between two wives is impossible and unattainable. Making this matter conditional upon something impossible to achieve is clear proof that it is not permitted in any way. Therefore only one wife is permitted for each person.

order.why: Read the supplied explanation of parental consent and family unity.
shortened: Baha'u'llah has clearly stated the consent of all living parents is required for a Baha'i marriage. This applies whether the parents are Baha'is or non-Baha'is divorced for years or not. This great law He has laid down to strengthen the social fabric, to knit closer the ties of the home, to place a certain gratitude and respect in the hearts of children for those who have given them life and sent their souls out on the eternal journey toward their Creator.

order.why: Retain the supplied historical wording concerning bigamy.
shortened: What I have said is that He has made bigamy bound on a precondition. As long as someone does not attain certitude regarding the capability to practice justice and his heart is not at rest that he can practice justice, he should not be intent upon a second marriage. But if he should be sure and attain certitude that he would practice justice on all levels (and conditions), then a second marriage is lawful.
(Our) purpose was to state that bigamy without justice is not lawful and that justice is very difficult (to achieve).

order.why: Keep the second supplied letter in its own terms.
Close with the authoritative clarification that monogamy is upheld.

questions: How does the image of two souls becoming united illuminate the practical conditions discussed here?
How can a family honor the couple’s freedom of choice while approaching parental consent with patience and care?
What might simplicity and restraint in financial expectations contribute to the beginning of a shared life?
What does the Qur’anic emphasis on companionship and mercy invite you to notice about the purposes of marriage law?
How does reading earlier provisions alongside authoritative interpretation change your understanding of gradual religious and social change?
What further questions arise when you connect these passages with spiritual partnership, prayer for married couples, and the responsibilities involved in divorce?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 30:21 · Companionship and mercy
references.note: In Mustafa Khattab’s translation, spouses, comfort, compassion, and mercy are presented as signs inviting reflection. Read this beside the compilation’s opening description of affinity and its concern for a household’s spiritual life. The comparison concerns the purposes and qualities of companionship; it does not make the legal provisions of the two traditions interchangeable.

references.label: 2 · The Kitáb-i-Aqdas, note 89 · Monogamy
references.note: The official note explains the gradual introduction of monogamy and quotes ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s authoritative interpretation: permission for a second wife was made dependent on an equity that cannot be fulfilled. Read this explanation alongside the earlier and apparently permissive statements retained in the compilation. It clarifies the intended law without altering the historical wording of those sources.

subjects.displayTitle: The Covenant: sustaining unity through difference
subjects.introduction: A Zoroastrian, a Siyyid, a mulla and a Jew seated together as one spirit: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá points to such gatherings as the plain evidence of what the Covenant can do. Bahá’u’lláh, He explains, saw how every religion of the past had splintered as each believer attributed his own new idea to God, and so with His own pen He appointed a Centre to whom all must turn, closing the door through which a thousand sects had once poured. The images He gives this provision are alive rather than merely legal: an artery pulsing through the body of the world, an ocean whose vastness invites the mightiest storms, a sheltering tree, a fortress no axe can reach. Yet the same guidance insists that no one can fully grasp revelation, that diversity of understanding is excellent, and that consultation is the community’s mainspring. Paul’s question to the Corinthians, whether Christ is divided, names the same danger of loyalties built around persons [1]. To go further is to consider firmness in the Covenant, the station and authority of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, and what it means to answer the call to unity.
subjects.arc: Begin with the fellowship made possible by the Covenant, examine its authority and protections, and conclude with independent investigation and diversity within unity.

order.why: Open with people crossing inherited religious barriers.
shortened: Consider what the power of the Covenant has done! It was an impossibility for a Zoroastrian to unite with a Siyyid and a mulla with a Jew. And for these to assemble with a Christian was an absolute impossibility. But the power of the Covenant has even so gathered them that they are accounted as one spirit. Although the bodies are numerous, the spirit is one.

order.why: Give unity the warmth of enduring companionship.
Hear the call of the Covenant as a melody of unity.
shortened: O friends! The call is the call of the Covenant and the melody is the melody of unity.

order.why: Explains the Covenant’s role in preserving unity and preventing division.
Introduce the image of an artery sustaining the whole.
shortened: Today the dynamic power of the world of existence is the power of the Covenant which like unto an artery pulsateth in the body of the contingent world and protecteth Baha'i unity.

The purpose of the Blessed Beauty in entering into this Covenant and Testament was to gather all existent beings around one point so that the thoughtless souls, who in every cycle and generation have been the cause of dissension, may not undermine the Cause. He hath, therefore, commanded that whatever emanateth from the Centre of the Covenant is right and is under His protection and favour, while all else is error.

order.why: Connect protection with fellowship between East and West.
shortened: The believers must realize that the Power of the Covenant is for the protection of the Cause of God, the promulgation of the religion of God and the brotherhood of the East and the West.

order.why: Extend the meaning of unity to the horizons.
shortened: Today the greatest of all affairs is the unity and oneness of the friends of God, and this unity and oneness is not possible except under the shadow of the standard of the Covenant. The unity of the Covenant is what causes the unity of the horizons.

order.why: Read the transformation of discord into a garden.
shortened: He hath subverted the foundations of discord and raised the edifice of divine favour. He hath kindled the light of guidance and, through the grace of the Abha Kingdom, turned the world into a garden of delights. He hath made manifest the Eternal Covenant and hath appeared, cup in hand, at the banquet of Revelation. He hath raised a mighty call and enabled every mindful soul to hear the celestial strains of the Covenant, so that the malicious might not breach the impregnable stronghold of the Cause or the ignorant taint its soft-flowing waters with the mire of idle fancies.

order.why: Approach the gathering together of souls through prayer.
shortened: Gather them, then, together around this Divine Law, the covenant of which Thou hast established with all Thy Prophets and Thy Messengers, and Whose ordinances Thou hast written down in Thy Tablets and Thy Scriptures.

order.why: Introduce the written provision for an authoritative center.
shortened: In brief, among the characteristics of this Dispensation which were not present in previous Dispensations, one is this: Baha'u'llah hath left no room for discord. For in His own blessed Day and by His Supreme Pen, He established a Covenant and Testament, appointed the Centre towards whom all must turn, explicitly specified the Interpreter of His Word, and closed the doors to false interpretations.

order.why: Read the historical argument for an explicit covenant.
shortened: It is clear and evident that in every cycle and dispensation an implicit statement was made in order to safeguard the Word of Oneness, to preserve the Cause of God from harm, and to ensure the unity of all that are gathered beneath the shadow of the Divine Tree, so that the impregnable stronghold of His Faith might remain safe and secure under the shadow of a single Word.

order.why: Examine the danger of attributing every new idea to God.
Consider the appointed center and the House of Justice.
shortened: Praise be to God, all such doors are closed in the Cause of Baha'u'llah for a special authoritative Center hath been appointed---a Center that solveth all difficulties and wardeth off all differences. The Universal House of Justice, likewise, wardeth off all differences and whatever it prescribeth must be accepted and he who transgresseth is rejected. But this Universal House of Justice which is the Legislature hath not yet been instituted.

order.why: Keep institutional authority beside non-interference in conscience.
Clarify ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s own statement of servitude.
shortened: For the sincere belief of 'Abdu'l-Baha is this: that the Primal Point, His Holiness the Exalted One - may my spirit be sacrificed for Him - is the Manifestation of Supreme Lordship and the Herald of the Beauty of Abha and the Sun of Truth and the Essence of Singleness and the Revelation of Divinity, the Most Great Luminary of the higher world, the Beauty of Abha, and 'Abdu'l-Baha is the weak, mortal servant of those two peerless Stars. This is the essence of my reality, the substance of my being, and the very nature of my identity.

order.why: Read interpretation as a protection against contention.
shortened: Therefore, in this day the doors of contention must be barred and the causes of strife prevented, and this is not possible unless all follow the Interpreter and obey the appointed Centre of the Covenant. That is, they must cleave unto his explicit utterance and hold fast unto his clear testimony in such wise that their tongues may relate only the words spoken by his tongue and their pens recount only that which he hath uttered.

order.why: Retain the reported procedure for disagreements.
shortened: Abdul Baha: First of all, the Blessed Beauty made this Covenant so that there should remain no differences. If there remain any disagreements amongst the friends, or differences as to the meaning of the Book - in whatever way there may arise any difference, Baha'u'llah says explicitly, 'turn to him (i.e., to the Center of the Covenant), whatever he says is correct; and after him to the House of Justice.' What is this for? It is to dispel differences.

order.why: Consider the limits of interpretation according to personal desire.
Hear the argument for fidelity to the designated interpreter.
shortened: Either one must say that the Blessed Beauty was, God forbid, ignorant and made a mistake in commanding all to obey the Center of the Covenant and explicitly confining the interpretation of the Book to the Center of the Covenant, or one must obey and turn to Him.

order.why: Read the strong formulation of obedience in that setting.
shortened: As for the matter of the Covenant, steadfastness in the Covenant means obedience - that no one should say "my opinion is this," rather they must obey whatever proceeds from the pen and tongue of the Center of the Covenant.

order.why: Keep the related reported warning against independent authority claims.
shortened: If a soul shall utter a word without the sanction of the Covenant, he is not firm. Baha'u'llah appointed a Covenant in order to ward off dissensions, so that no one should give his own opinion, but that the Center should be referred to.

order.why: Retain the report’s contrast with Christian history as an attributed claim.
shortened: Baha'u'llah appointed a Covenant to ward off dissensions: so that no one can have his own opinion--so that the Center can be referred to. There were dissensions in the time of Christ because there was no Center.

order.why: Read the provision against speaking on one’s own behalf.
shortened: The Blessed Beauty has left no room for any one to weaken (the Cause). He entered into this Covenant to preserve the Baha'i Unity so that no one might say anything on his own behalf.

order.why: Concentrate the argument into a shared point of reference.
shortened: You see how many sects and religions appeared after Christ. Now the Blessed Beauty has designated one point so that no differences would remain.

order.why: Keep the historically present center in view.
Join obedience with gathering together.
Hear the concise warning against disruption.
Ask what sustains the movement of a united community.
shortened: In sum, Baha'i unity cannot be preserved save through the Covenant of God. In this day, the dynamic power in the body of the world is the Covenant; if the Covenant be neglected, what other power can move it? The statement reportedly uttered by Christ to Peter, "Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church", preserved Christian unity for a thousand years.

order.why: Read the warning about rapid fragmentation.
Consider the image of an impregnable fort.
shortened: Were it not for the protecting power of the Covenant to guard the impregnable fort of the Cause of GOD there would arise among the Bahais, in a day, a thousand different sects as was the case in former ages, but in this Blessed Dispensation, for the sake of the permanency of the Cause of GOD and the avoidance of dissension amongst the people of GOD, the Blessed Beauty (May my soul be a sacrifice to HIM), has through the Supreme Pen written the Covenant and Testament; He appointed a Center, the Exponent of the Book and the Annuller of disputes.

order.why: Retain the stated consequences of competing personal positions.
shortened: The power of the Covenant firmly establishes and preserves Baha'i unity; otherwise the Baha'i Cause would be completely disrupted, each soul would find a particular opinion, and the Cause of God would be totally obliterated and destroyed.

order.why: Read adherence as the condition of preservation.
shortened: The protection of the Cause of God and the unity of the people of Baha are dependent on firmness in the Covenant of God and adherence to the writings of the Expounder of the divine verses. Apart from this, every hope will end in despair, and every remark will lead to toil and abasement.

order.why: Keep the foundation of religion beside unity.
shortened: For firmness in the Covenant will preserve the unity of the religion of God and the foundation of the religion of God will not be shaken.

order.why: Read firmness as a condition for a larger spiritual purpose.
shortened: The first condition is firmness in the Covenant of God. For the power of the Covenant will protect the Cause of Baha'u'llah from the doubts of the people of error. It is the fortified fortress of the Cause of God and the firm pillar of the religion of God. Today no power can conserve the oneness of the Baha'i world save the Covenant of God; otherwise differences like unto a most great tempest will encompass the Baha'i world. It is evident that the axis of the oneness of the world of humanity is the power of the Covenant and nothing else.

order.why: Introduce the mountain image of steadfastness.
shortened: Today the most important principle of faith is firmness in the Covenant, because firmness in the Covenant wards off differences. Therefore, you must be firm as mountains.

order.why: Retain the brief parallel and its visible omission.
Read the divine institution and its confirmations.
shortened: For this Divine Covenant is the Institution of the Lord. The Blessed Perfection in all the Tablets, Books, epistles and supplication has begged confirmation for and has praised and commended those who are firm in this Covenant and the Testament and has asked the wrath of God and woe and desolation and His Vengeance unto the violators. For firmness in this Covenant will preserve the unity of the religion of God and the Foundation of the religion of God will not be shaken.

order.why: Move from principle into action and testing.
shortened: Now is the time for the field of action and testing of men, for the mighty edifice of God's Cause rests upon the pillar of the Covenant and Testament, and the heaven of God's religion is illumined and radiant through the star of the Covenant.

God forbid that if some ungrateful person should assault this pillar, not a single nail would remain to uphold the divine pavilion and the merciful tabernacle, not a single lamp would remain lit in the divine gathering. The House of God would be buried from its very foundation, the Cycle would become futile and the laws nullified.

order.why: Notice the sacrifices involved in keeping the Word whole.
shortened: Ye have not permitted the Designated Station to be humbled, nor been willing to see the Centre of Authority discredited or exposed to mockery and persecution. Ye have striven to keep the Word whole and one. Ye have passed through the portals of mercy. Ye have not let the Blessed Beauty slip from your minds, to fade unremembered.'

order.why: Consider the vulnerability imagined without a strong center.
shortened: God forbid that if any weakness or languor should occur in the Center of the Covenant, how would Baha'i unity be preserved and how would the teachings of the Blessed Beauty be promoted?

order.why: Keep the recorded discourse’s historical setting.
Examine how prejudice and private imagination can obstruct growth.
shortened: True Religion has nothing to do with human imagination. God's Will is independent of human opinion.Personal ideas and mere human prejudice are the great obstacles to spiritual growth.

When there is difference of view there is absence of the Spirit. The Word is the only Standard of Truth. Discord and disagreement are impossible among those who adhere to the Manifestation and sever themselves from human opinion.'

order.why: Read the difficult language of exclusion in its protective argument.
shortened: The Blessed Beauty entered into this Covenant for obedience and not for opposition. I say this merely for the protection of the Cause of God and for the purpose of safeguarding unity among the friends. Were it not for the removal of vain imaginings and the eradication of differences, I should not have asserted that I am 'the Center of the Covenant'.

order.why: Retain the stern call in its historical conflict.
shortened: However, you must be so firm and steadfast in the Covenant and Testament that the Covenant-breakers cannot draw a breath in any gathering where you are present. Today, the magnet that attracts the confirmations of the Kingdom of God is firmness in the Covenant and Testament, and all else is delirious talk. For by what means can Baha'i unity be preserved? Is it through the nonsensical utterances of some? God forbid!

order.why: Keep the polemical allegations attributed to their reported source.
shortened: Similarly, had it not been for the power of the Covenant after the ascension of the Ancient Beauty, it is evident what the people would have done, how they would have spent their time, like Mirza Yahya, taking many wives and satisfying their lusts and desires. They would have destroyed the divine standard.

order.why: Consider the ocean and foam image without adopting its polemics as neutral history.
shortened: The Covenant is like an ocean that preserves Baha'i unity, and these souls are like foam - they make temporary movements but like Judas Iscariot and Judas' helpers and those who agreed with Judas, they will soon be forgotten like the foam of the sea. But the ocean of the Covenant remains established, for it preserves Baha'i unity.

order.why: Read opposition through the ship and tree images.
shortened: It is clear and evident that every mighty cause in existence must face intense opposition, and every sturdy ship must encounter massive waves. Similarly, such a Covenant will find violators of utmost strength, and such an ancient Testament will face opponents of greatest power. The vaster the ocean, the mightier its tempests; the firmer the edifice, the more exposed it is to the force of hurricanes.

order.why: Keep the particular image of defense.
shortened: That brave lion is the Lion of the Covenant who with one movement caused that creature filled with hatred to fall to the ground, and the Blessed Tree remained established in its place.

order.why: Hear the assurance of endurance.
Return to the relationship between authority and unifying power.
shortened: And that instantaneously effective compound is the Covenant, whose sanctifying lights shine forth upon the horizons.

The specifically designated Center of Authority was established, the clear and manifest Interpreter of verses was made known, the Remover of differences was mentioned, and the medicine and remedy were entrusted to the designated skilled Physician.

order.why: Receive guidance as light in darkness.
shortened: We praise and thank Him for His grace, His generosity, and His beneficence, and for having made clear to us His straight path, expanded for us the upright way, given us a light by which we are guided in the darkest night, ordained for us the mighty Covenant, and clearly established through His Supreme Pen the appointed Center, firm as an impregnable fortress, the Interpreter of His verses, the Expositor of His words, the Solver of complex problems, the Remover of doubts of both past and present, the Eliminator of differences from all directions.

order.why: Turn the work of protection into supplication.
Close the linked passages with gratitude beneath the tree.
shortened: O servant of God! Thanks be to the Most Great Unity that thou hast been gathered beneath the shade of the Tree of the Covenant, that He hath illumined thy heart with the light of the bounty of the Luminary of the horizons, and that thou hast become assured of the verses of divine unity.

order.why: Read the supplied account of continuing authority.
Locate that authority within the purposes of revelation.
Consider integrity and expansion together.
Keep the supplied warning about forcing personal preferences upon the whole.
Invite younger readers to ponder the hub of the community.
Read the warning about limited human reasoning.
Connect protection from fragmentation with humanity’s oneness.
End with independent investigation, diverse understanding and mature consultation.

questions: What do the images of an artery, an ocean, and a sheltering tree reveal about different dimensions of the Covenant?
How can a common source of authority enable people from formerly divided communities to work together?
What distinguishes offering an understanding in consultation from making one’s understanding binding on everyone else?
How does Paul’s question about factions illuminate the danger of organizing a religious community around personal loyalties?
How might the final passage’s account of independent investigation shape your reading of the stronger statements about obedience?
What practices could help a community combine firmness in the Covenant with humility, freedom of conscience, and a growing capacity to consult?

references.label: 1 · 1 Corinthians 1:10–17 · A community divided by loyalties
references.note: Paul addresses contentions among people identifying themselves with Paul, Apollos, Cephas, or Christ, and asks whether Christ is divided. Compare his concern about personal affiliations with the compilation’s concern for a common center and the integrity of a religious community. The parallel identifies a shared problem of fragmentation; it does not establish identical arrangements of interpretation or succession.

subjects.displayTitle: A second birth: awakening to another life
subjects.introduction: Go home, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá told departing pilgrims, and let everyone see the change in you: greater love, greater joy, greater kindness and forbearance. A second birth, in His teaching, is not a private feeling but a visible fact, the dark made luminous, the heedless made aware, the robber made trustworthy. To be born of the Spirit is to pass in the same way out of the matrix of nature into the Kingdom, and to find oneself with a new eye, a new ear, a new heart. Jesus’ night conversation with Nicodemus is the text these interpretations keep returning to. The image also consoles the bereaved, since the next world stands to this one as this one stood to the womb. From here the journey leads to the Holy Spirit as the agent of this change, to spiritual baptism by water and fire, and to the slow, daily work of spiritual transformation that follows an awakening.
subjects.arc: Begin with the visible fruits of renewal, explore the birth analogy and its scriptural roots, and follow awakening into growth, service, and hope beyond death.

order.why: Turn to the central scriptural interpretation.
shortened: Even as Jesus said: "Ye must be born again." Again He saith: "Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the Kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." The purport of these words is that whosoever in every dispensation is born of the Spirit and is quickened by the breath of the Manifestation of Holiness, he verily is of those that have attained unto "life" and "resurrection" and have entered into the "paradise" of the love of God.

order.why: Name the social and ethical realities of new life.
shortened: Reality is the love of God, reality is the knowledge of God, reality is the second birth, reality is receiving the breaths of the Holy Spirit, reality is the oneness of humanity, reality is fellowship between people, reality is friendship, reality is justice, reality is equality between people.

order.why: Open with the change others should experience.
shortened: When you return to America everybody must see the greatest change in you. You must show that you have had a second birth. You must show the greatest love and the greatest joy. You must show the greatest kindness and forbearance; in fact, you must show complete severance and humility, so that when you enter a meeting all will see the change in you."

order.why: Introduce awakening through paired transformations.
shortened: Existential rewards consist in the virtues and perfections that adorn the human reality. For example, man was immersed in darkness and becomes luminous; he was ignorant and becomes informed; he was heedless and becomes aware; he was asleep and is awakened; he was dead and is quickened to life; he was blind and begins to see; he was deaf and begins to hear; he was earthly and becomes heavenly; he was material and becomes spiritual. Through these rewards he is reborn in spirit, is created anew, and becomes the manifestation of the verse in the Gospel that says that the Apostles "were born, not of blood, nor of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God"--that is, they were delivered from the animal characteristics and qualities that are inherent to human nature and acquired divine attributes, which are the outpouring grace of God. This is the true meaning of being born again.

order.why: Read renewal through changed character.
Consider the striking examples of transformation.
Read the signs of regeneration beside the virtues just described.
shortened: By these things you know the faithful servant of God. How do we know the light? By its rays. So when you see these qualities, you will know that the servant of God has received the regeneration--you must be born once again. You must pray and supplicate, and the more you pray and supplicate, the nearer you will be to God.

order.why: Explore the child’s entrance into a wider world.
shortened: The sacred Books of all nations speak of the possibility of the new birth of man. What does this mean? A child in the womb of its mother is in utter darkness. When it is born into the world it comes into the Light. While in the womb it cannot understand the use of its faculties, but when it comes into the phenomenal world, then is understood the use of hearing, speech, sight, etc.

order.why: Develop the relation between faculties and their new use.
shortened: Before his first or physical birth man was in the world of the matrix. He had no knowledge of this world; his eyes could not see; his ears could not hear. When he was born from the world of the matrix, he beheld another world.

Similarly, as long as man is in the matrix of the human world, as long as he is the captive of nature, he is out of touch and without knowledge of the universe of the Kingdom. If he attains rebirth while in the world of nature, he will become informed of the divine world.

order.why: Retain the parallel account in its own wording.
shortened: A child in the matrix of its mother is in utter darkness. When it is born into the world it comes into the light. While in the matrix it cannot understand the uses of its faculties; but when it comes into the phenomenal world then the uses of hearing, speech, sight, etc., are understood.
The new birth is realized in this world when we become characterized with the characteristics of God, when His name and attributes become our name and attributes.

order.why: Keep the concise movement from physical to spiritual light.
shortened: As the babe is born into the light of this physical world, so must the physical and intellectual man be born into the light of the world of Divinity.

order.why: Consider release from limitation through the birth analogy.
Read the explicit spiritual application of the analogy.
Ask what enables knowledge of another order of existence.
Distinguish inability to grasp from proof of nonexistence.
Read present life as preparation and beginning.
shortened: This is the matrix world for the soul, even as the womb was the matrix world for the body or vehicle. - Birth into consciousness of another world begins here, a world for which this physical and material one is but the preparation and foundation."

order.why: Concentrate the contrast between universe and kingdom.
shortened: When a man is born into the world of phenomena he finds the universe; when he is born from this world to the world of the spirit, he finds the Kingdom.'

order.why: Keep intellectual and spiritual capacities together.
shortened: Just as man has been physically born into this world, he may be reborn from the realm and matrix of nature, for the realm of nature is a condition of animalism, darkness and defect. In this second birth he attains the world of the Kingdom. There he witnesses and realizes that the world of nature is a world of gloom, whereas the Kingdom is a world of radiance; the world of nature is a world of defects, the Kingdom is a realm of perfection; the world of nature is a world without enlightenment, the Kingdom of spiritual humanity is a heaven of illumination.

order.why: Read the animal contrast within its moral argument.
shortened: Until man is born again from the world of nature, that is to say, becomes detached from the world of nature, he is essentially an animal, and it is the teachings of God which convert this animal into a human soul.

order.why: Examine the strengthening of the spiritual aspect.
Keep the parallel formulation distinct.
Connect rebirth with baptism through the Holy Spirit.
Explains second birth as spiritual quickening through the Holy Spirit.
Read water and fire as language of divine life and love.
shortened: Jesus Christ said that we should be born again through the spiritual fire and love of God and be baptized by the water of life and the Holy Spirit, that we may obtain everlasting life.

order.why: Hear the invitation to seek that baptism.
shortened: Thou shalt receive baptism with the spirit of life and the fire of the love of God, seek second birth from the realm of nature, and attain eternal life.

order.why: Receive the account of those already renewed.
Let the call’s image of circulation connect persons and the whole.
shortened: The call of the Abha Kingdom penetrates swiftly like spirit through veins, arteries, hearts and souls, creating a new creation and baptizing with water, spirit and fire. A second birth takes place and a new creation is raised up.

order.why: Distinguish existence from spiritual creation.
shortened: As for spiritual creation, which is the station of the new creation, it is supreme guidance, eternal life, universal qualities, the acquirement of the all-inclusive divine perfections, and progress in all the stages of human endowments. This creation and existence is realized through the appearance of the Divine Manifestations in the contingent world.

order.why: Read beginnings in relation to the advent of revelation.
shortened: However, the "beginning" mentioned in the Holy Books refers to the beginning of Manifestation, and "creation" refers to the second spiritual birth, as Christ said, "Ye must be born again." Without doubt, the beginning of this spiritual creation was the Manifestation itself in every age and cycle, for each Manifestation of Truth is Adam, and the first to believe in Him is Eve, and all souls who are born with the second spiritual birth are their children and descendants.

order.why: Set renewal within the purpose of the Manifestations.
shortened: Nay, rather, Christ appeared in order to illumine the world of humanity, to render the earthly world celestial, to make the human kingdom a realm of angels, to unite the hearts, to enkindle the light of love in human souls, so that such souls might become independent, attaining complete unity and fellowship, turning to God, entering into the divine Kingdom, receiving the bounties and bestowals of God and partaking of the manna from heaven. Through Christ they were intended to be baptized by the Holy Spirit, attain a new spirit and realize the everlasting life.

order.why: Trace the relation between the Word, the Kingdom and eternal life.
shortened: In brief: the people of the world are in need of eternal life, and eternal life depends on the manifestation of the Kingdom, and the manifestation of the Kingdom depends on the penetration of the Word of God and the confirmation of the Holy Spirit - that is, it depends on the divine power that brings the dead to life, makes the blind see and the deaf hear, and fulfills the second birth mentioned in the Gospel text: "That which is born of flesh is flesh, and that which is born of spirit is spirit. You must be born again."
The human spirit attains eternity through faith and second birth.

order.why: Consider faith as second birth and enduring life.
shortened: Faith is mentioned in the Scriptures as the 'Second Birth' or 'Everlasting Life.' In this day it is the Spirit of God, the real true belief.

order.why: Retain the particular exhortation to religious recognition.
Read the protective vesture in its revealed context.
Hear the invitation to drink the water of life.
Let the trumpet image interrupt spiritual sleep.
Consider the dawn of illumination.
Read the movement from scattered drops to abundant rain.
shortened: Your faith comes like rain; the first drops are far between, but soon it will pour in torrents.
You must be reborn by the Spirit. A child in the matrix has eyes and ears but only learns their use when it is born. A man cannot comprehend the Spirit before he has put aside earthly things.

order.why: Acknowledge difficulty in the beginning of belief.
Join the new beginning to daily growth.
Examine freedom from captivity to desire.
Keep the devotional practice and its source omission visible.
Read the life of the Covenant through freedom from harshness.
shortened: Today the pulsating power in the arteries of the body of the world is the spirit of the Covenant—the spirit which is the cause of life. Whosoever is vivified with this spirit the freshness and beauty of life become manifest in him, he is baptized with the Holy Spirit, he is born again, is freed from oppression and tyranny, from heedlessness and harshness which deaden the spirit, and attains to everlasting life.

order.why: Consider the capacities made visible in a renewed person.
Turn recognition into gratitude.
Read the personal assurance of opened insight.
Keep the direct application of the Gospel’s imagery.
Receive the prayer for heavenly life.
Carry renewal into freeing and gladdening other souls.
shortened: It is my hope that that thou mayest find ease and comfort, and that, with a heart assured and a spirit rejoiced with the outpourings of His grace, thou mayest deliver the glad-tidings of the Abha Kingdom, free the souls from the darkness of the world of nature, and lead them to the splendorous light of the Kingdom--that is, that thou mayest help them to be born again from the darksome womb of nature and baptize them with the Holy Spirit, with the fire of the love of God, and with the water of life.

order.why: Read the image’s use in consolation for a bereaved mother.
shortened: Now he has stepped from the matrix of this world into the realm eternal. This is the second birth referred to by Jesus Christ.

order.why: Keep the recorded answer about the departed within its particular question.
shortened: To the first part of the question he answered: "No. They have no power to influence the world of men and only those who in life had been among the spiritually regenerated ones, those who had been re-born or baptized of the Holy Spirit, only such souls could consciously communicate or have knowledge of things in this world."

order.why: Offer thanks for the living waters.
shortened: I render Thee thanks, therefore, and extol Thee, in the name of all them that are dear to Thee, for that Thou hast caused them to be born again, by reason of the living waters which have flowed down out of the mouth of Thy will.

order.why: Close the linked sources with the blessing on awakening.
shortened: Blessed is he who hath attained on this day to the lights of Our Name, the Self-Subsisting, and who hath been stirred by the breaths of revelation and risen from among the dead. And blessed is he who hath been born anew through the verses of his Lord, the Lord of all beings, and soared in this atmosphere wherefrom the wings of birds are barred.

order.why: Read the supplied vision of renewal beyond human divisions.
shortened: Such a firm foundation cannot be impregnated into human consciousness save by one universal and all-pervasive power, for every other power is helpless except for the power of the Holy Spirit. The outpourings of the Holy Spirit are such that they can transform man, imbuing him with all the virtues, bestowing upon him the second birth, baptizing him with the fire of the love of God, which is love for all created things, and quickening him with the water of eternal life, and the Holy Spirit itself.

order.why: End with the supplied account of purification and its demands.

questions: What changes in conduct make spiritual renewal recognizable to someone who does not share the same religious vocabulary?
How does the birth analogy illuminate both continuity with a former life and entry into something previously unimagined?
What does Jesus’ exchange with Nicodemus suggest about the limits of taking spiritual language only literally?
How can a decisive awakening and patient daily growth belong to the same process?
What distinguishes freedom from domination by desire from withdrawal from the needs and responsibilities of the world?
How might the connected subjects of baptism, the Holy Spirit, and spiritual transformation deepen the way you understand a second birth?

references.label: 1 · John 3:1–8 · Jesus and Nicodemus
references.note: Nicodemus hears the language of being born again and asks about another physical birth. Jesus speaks of water and Spirit and offers the image of wind whose movement is heard without being fully traced. Read the passage in its own setting, then compare the compilation’s interpretations through spiritual perception, transformed conduct, and entry into a wider life. The comparison opens the metaphor without assuming that all Christian understandings of baptism are the same.

subjects.displayTitle: A renewed humanity: character and civilization
subjects.introduction: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s hope for a new humanity sounds, at first, almost modest: that you will never harm a neighbour or speak ill of anyone, that you will care more for the interests of others than your own, and that someone who has failed a hundred thousand times will still turn to you expecting forgiveness. Yet from such conduct He expects nothing less than a world made over. He pictures a spiritual spring in which this lowly earth becomes the Abhá Kingdom, a stone polished until it mirrors the sun, and the hearts of all mankind beating as a single heart; the New Jerusalem of the Bible, He says, is simply divine civilization, and it is ready now. The letter to the Ephesians traces the same movement from a renewed self to truthful speech, honest work, giving and forgiveness [1]. The talk of a new race of men belongs to this spiritual and social purpose, not to biology or a timetable, and Shoghi Effendi and the Universal House of Justice describe the change as gradual, collective and still being learned. The way forward opens onto the maturity of mankind, the economic problem and its solution, and the foundations of a future civilization built on the oneness of humanity.
subjects.arc: Begin with the conduct of a renewed person, widen toward cities and world society, and conclude with gradual collective work and humility about the future.

order.why: Distinguish living change from fruitless dogmatism.
shortened: The morals of humanity must undergo change. New remedies and solutions for human problems must be adopted. Human intellects themselves must change and be subject to the universal reformation. Just as the thoughts and hypotheses of past ages are fruitless today, likewise dogmas and codes of human invention are obsolete and barren of product in religion. Nay, it is true that they are the cause of enmity and conducive to strife in the world of humanity; war and bloodshed proceed from them, and the oneness of mankind finds no recognition in their observance.

order.why: Open with justice and care in daily relations.
Make forgiveness the demanding test of renewal.
shortened: O ye friends of God! Show ye an endeavor that all the nations and communities of the world, even the enemies, put their trust, assurance and hope in you; that if a person falls into errors for a hundred-thousand times he may yet turn his face to you, hopeful that you will forgive his sins; for he must not become hopeless, neither grieved nor despondent. This is the conduct and the manner of the people of Baha'.

order.why: Read character as the realization of spiritual teaching.
shortened: The essential thing is that we must all strive with heart and soul so that the reality of divine attributes may become manifest in the realm of possibility, and the human world may become a mirror of the Most Great Beauty. Faith, certitude, mystic knowledge, truth, integrity, reconciliation, worship of truth, love, oneness, fellowship and wisdom may become realized and renowned among all peoples.

order.why: Imagine excellence that includes tenderness and sociability.
Hold material and spiritual accomplishment together.
Consider the stone polished until it reflects light.
shortened: The more the world of humanity develops, the more the effulgences or emanations of Divinity will become revealed, just as the stone, when it becomes polished and pure as a mirror, will reflect in fuller degree the glory and splendor of the sun.

order.why: Connect lived teachings with a transformed world.
Introduce the image of spiritual spring.
Extend the spring to every region.
shortened: The lights of truth will shine forth, the mysteries of truth will become clear and evident, the flowers of the divine garden will bloom, and the springtime of the All-Merciful will encompass all regions and realms.

order.why: Read illumination through mind and thought.
shortened: Today the world and the people are under the shadow of divine providence, the light of the Sun of Reality hath been shed upon the world of minds and thoughts; hence, light is seen everywhere.

order.why: Hear the call that quickens hearts and consciences.
Relate new teachings to the needs of the age.
Read transformation through the fire of wisdom and the Word.
Set spiritual virtues within the purpose of the Prophets.
shortened: All the Prophets and Messengers were sent by the Lord of the worlds so that, through the endeavors of those holy souls, the suns of spiritual virtues might shine forth from the horizons of human temples.

order.why: Consider the capacities evoked by the divine breath.
shortened: Within the very breath of such souls as are pure and sanctified far-reaching potentialities are hidden. So great are these potentialities that they exercise their influence upon all created things.

order.why: Read fragrance and sight as invitations to recognition.
shortened: Today the divine fragrance is wafting from the garment of His Cause - surely every possessor of smell perceives it. The Sun of the Countenance is manifest and shining from the horizon of appearance - every possessor of sight beholds it.

order.why: Let the hope for new people take the form of prayer.
shortened: Be not grieved by the loss of the steadfast ones or the turning away of the deniers, for through prayer a people shall be raised up who will place the foot of detachment upon all who are in the heavens and the earth, who will shake the sleeve of sanctification over all that hath been created of water and clay, and who will hasten toward the Friend, heedless of self.

order.why: Move from competing identities toward love and oneness.
shortened: How good it is if the friends be as close as sheaves of light, if they stand together side by side in a firm unbroken line. For now have the rays of reality from the Sun of the world of existence, united in adoration all the worshippers of this light; and these rays have, through infinite grace, gathered all peoples together within this wide-spreading shelter; therefore must all souls become as one soul, and all hearts as one heart. Let all be set free from the multiple identities that were born of passion and desire, and in the oneness of their love for God find a new way of life.

order.why: Consider children belonging beyond geographic divisions.
shortened: These children are neither Oriental nor Occidental, neither Asiatic nor American, neither European nor African, but they are of the Kingdom; their native home is heaven and their resort is the Kingdom of ABHA.

order.why: Read the human family through the image of one flock.
shortened: Therefore the members of the world of humanity must embrace each other with utmost love and conciliation and under the protection of this Shepherd these sheep may graze in the meadow of Clemency and while they grow and develop acquire infinite joy and happiness.

order.why: See a gathering as a possible prototype of humanity.
shortened: This assembly is an example of how in the future, the whole of humanity will enter beneath the tabernacle [of the Cause], rest under the shadow of a single tree, drink from the same chalice and be satisfied from the same fountainhead. The effect of such gatherings will be manifested at a future time and will attract divine confirmations.

order.why: Read the gathered community through the divine image and moral qualities.
Make the individual a light within the gathering.
shortened: Be a candle for the gathering and cause the kindling of the Fire of God, blazing in the hearts and souls of the people of East and West.

order.why: Carry that light into a wider society.
Read the promise of a contribution still unfolding.
Imagine a city through its knowledge, practice and praise.
shortened: God should be commemorated in every city; the lights of guidance should be diffused; the souls should be attracted to the beauty of God; the doors of knowledge should be opened; the teachings of God should be practiced -- and the tongues should be eloquent in the praise of God. When these virtues become apparent within a city, the heavenly manna will descend, and that city -- wherever it may be -- will become a New Jerusalem.

order.why: Interpret New Jerusalem as divine civilization in the reported account.
shortened: Material civilization has reached an advanced plane, but now there is need of spiritual civilization. Material civilization alone will not satisfy; it cannot meet the conditions and requirements of the present age; its benefits are limited to the world of matter.
The heavenly Jerusalem is none other than divine civilization, and it is now ready. It is to be and shall be organized, and the oneness of humankind will be a visible fact.

order.why: Explains why outward progress requires renewal in the human spirit.
Widen the circle into a shared human heartbeat.
Read the world as a mirror of spiritual qualities.
shortened: The world of creation is advancing and the Orb of the horizons is in full splendor. Though the Sun of Truth be hidden behind the clouds of glory, yet its effulgence and rays are continuous and successive. The surface of the earth shall soon become a supreme paradise through divine bestowals, and the dusty realm shall become a mirror of the most exalted heights. The images of the Kingdom shall be reflected in the mirror of the world, and the grace of the Realm of Might shall become manifest and embodied.

order.why: Connect the renewal of persons with peace in the world.
Imagine the moral capacities of public leadership.
Let the pen and worldwide concern reshape national aspiration.
Ask what material civilization alone leaves unresolved.
Consider sensitivity to wealth beside poverty.
Keep intentions and peace together.
Read the reported hope for international justice.
shortened: The bright day is coming. The nucleus of the new race is forming. The harbinger of the new ideals of international justice is appearing. The trees of hope will become verdant; the copper of scorn and derision will be transmuted into the gold of honor and praise; the arid desert of ignorance will be transformed into the luxuriant garden of knowledge, the threatening clouds shall be dispelled and the stars of faith and charity will again twinkle in the clear heaven of human consciousness.

order.why: Retain the historically situated expectation of a new age.
shortened: Therefore, this twentieth century is the dawn, or beginning, of spiritual illumination, and it is evident that day by day it will advance. It will reach such a degree that spiritual effulgences will overcome the physical, so that divine susceptibilities will overpower material intelligence and the heavenly light dispel and banish earthly darkness.

Among the results of the manifestation of spiritual forces will be that the human world will adapt itself to a new social form, the justice of God will become manifest throughout human affairs, and human equality will be universally established.

order.why: Read regeneration through thought and ideals.
shortened: Sanctified and holy thou must occupy thy time with the diffusion of the Lights of the Kingdom, strive in the enkindlement of the hearts and the regeneration of the souls. Thou must be the servant of the Blessed Beauty and create a great reverberation in the spheres of thoughts and ideals.

order.why: Understand the reported new race through spiritual consciousness.
shortened: A new era of divine consciousness is upon us. The world of humanity is going through a process of transformation. A new race is being developed.

order.why: Keep the prospect of continuing spiritual progress.
Consider the relation between an age’s capacity and its teachings.
shortened: Baha'Ullah has a larger message on a greater number of subjects than any other, just as this is an age more ready, because of the great spiritual advance made in the great kingdom of knowledge, to understand and benefit by his just commands.

order.why: Join the horizons of East and West.
Read the reported claim about spiritual life and public affairs.
