Hear the appeal to contribute comfort and effort to civilization.
shortened: What is the soul but to be offered in the arena of Truth, what is the spirit but to be given up for the progress of divine Civilization and universal Peace, and what is rest and comfort but to be thrown away for the establishment of brotherhood and the spiritualization of mankind!

order.why: Imagine education extending care even to an enemy.
Allow the explicitly stated possibility of successive centuries.
shortened: The teachings of the Ancient Beauty constitute that Covenant, all of which must needs be realized in its own time, even though it may take successive centuries; yet ultimately it must be fulfilled and breathe a new spirit into the dead bodies of mankind.

order.why: Retain the reported image of profound structural change.
Read the fire of love moving across regions.
shortened: Now, praise be to God, the fire of the love of God has been kindled in the censer of Iran, and its world-illumining flame has reached the western countries. Since this divine kindled fire has begun to blaze in those vast countries, it will become more aflame day by day, and by divine help and favor its fire will spread to all directions.

order.why: Close the linked sources with a future hunger for wisdom.
Preserve the supplied prophetic images in their own register.
shortened: "There lay concealed within the Holy Veil, and prepared for the service of God, a company of His chosen ones who shall be manifested unto men, who shall aid His Cause, who shall be afraid of no one, though the entire human race rise up and war against them. These are the ones who, before the gaze of the dwellers on earth and the denizens of heaven, shall arise and, shouting aloud, acclaim the name of the Almighty, and summon the children of men to the path of God, the All-Glorious, the All-Praised."         "The day is approaching when God will have, by an act of His Will, raised up a race of men the nature of which is inscrutable to all save God, the All-Powerful, the Self-Subsisting."

order.why: Keep the short supplied formulation and its omissions visible.
Read the pilgrim-note account with its limited authority.
Retain the reported speculation without making it an editorial prediction.
Consider the supplied image of a society in fermentation.
Read the scale of transformation being anticipated.
Distinguish successive stages in the account of a future commonwealth.
shortened: Suffice it to say that this consummation will, by its very nature, be a gradual process, and must, as Baha'u'llah has Himself anticipated, lead at first to the establishment of that Lesser Peace which the nations of the earth, as yet unconscious of His Revelation and yet unwittingly enforcing the general principles which He has enunciated, will themselves establish. This momentous and historic step, involving the reconstruction of mankind, as the result of the universal recognition of its oneness and wholeness, will bring in its wake the spiritualization of the masses, consequent to the recognition of the character, and the acknowledgment of the claims, of the Faith of Baha'u'llah -- the essential condition to that ultimate fusion of all races, creeds, classes, and nations which must signalize the emergence of His New World Order.

order.why: Consider the difficulties of learning community life.
Connect universal consciousness with a new way of living.
shortened: The teachings of Baha'u'llah will establish a new way of life for humanity.
Divisional attachments are of man, while universal service is of God. The Guardian is now anxious that all the friends achieve a universal consciousness and a universal way of life.

order.why: Read moral guidance through the renewal of spiritual values.
Welcome useful new methods as part of a dynamic culture.
Join institutional justice, material improvement and grassroots development.
Locate transformation in collective efforts to develop capacities.
Close with humility about the sequence of humanity’s future.

questions: Which qualities described here would most change the experience of meeting another person?
How might inner transformation and changes in social institutions strengthen or frustrate each other?
What does the Ephesians passage contribute by linking a renewed life to speech, work, generosity, and forgiveness?
How can images of a new humanity inspire action while preserving the dignity and diversity of people as they are?
What can the passages about gradual development and uncertainty teach us about reading confident hopes for the future?
Where might a community begin to connect spiritual growth, economic justice, and the practical learning needed for a more united civilization?

references.label: 1 · Ephesians 4:22–32 · Renewal made practical
references.note: The letter moves from putting on a renewed humanity to concrete conduct: truthful speech, useful work that enables giving, words that help others, kindness, and forgiveness. Read this movement beside the compilation’s relationship between character and civilization. Both make renewal visible in relationships; the comparison leaves room to examine their distinct accounts of religious community and wider social change.

subjects.displayTitle: A shared language: understanding across borders
subjects.introduction: A traveller enters a strange city and feels he has come home, because every voice around him can be understood. That is the promise ‘Abdu’l-Bahá drew from Bahá’u’lláh’s call to the parliaments of the world to choose one language and one script for all. Each child would learn two tongues: the mother tongue that carries a people’s inheritance, and an auxiliary language that opens the whole earth. Language, He explained, exists to convey the secrets of one heart to another; without a shared medium, the sciences cannot travel freely and the Most Great Peace cannot be firmly established. He welcomed Esperanto as a beginning while asking that it go on being perfected, and He looked to a gathering of the nations to make the final choice. The story of Pentecost offers a different picture, of many listeners each hearing the message in their own language [1]. This hope leads naturally to the oneness of humanity, to the unity of hearts it presupposes, and to the means of building a future civilization in which speech becomes a servant of love.
subjects.arc: Begin with the possibility of direct understanding, examine collective choice and education, read the Esperanto discussions in context, and return to language’s human purpose.

order.why: Connect communication with the disclosure of hearts and the spread of knowledge.
shortened: Unless the unity of languages is realized, the Most Great Peace and the oneness of the human world cannot be effectively organized and established because the function of language is to portray the mysteries and secrets of human hearts.

Therefore, the very first service to the world of man is to establish this auxiliary international means of communication. It will become the cause of the tranquillity of the human commonwealth. Through it sciences and arts will be spread among the nations, and it will prove to be the means of the progress and development of all races.

order.why: Open with the delight of being able to speak together.
Ask what lies deeper than outward words.
Imagine arriving in another city as in one’s own home.
shortened: It is observed that due to the diversity of languages among the peoples of the earth, most nations are deprived of association, fellowship, and the acquisition of knowledge and wisdom from one another. Therefore, through pure bounty and grace, all are commanded to choose a language - whether newly created or selected from existing tongues of the earth - and all shall speak it. In this way, the whole earth shall be seen as one city, for all will understand each other's speech and comprehend one another's intent. This is the cause of the world's advancement and elevation. Should a person journey from his homeland and enter any city, it would be as though he had entered his own dwelling.

order.why: State the pairing of mother tongue and auxiliary language.
Defines an auxiliary language as a second language alongside the native tongue.
Keep the reported affirmation of linguistic diversity nearby.
Read the two-language educational proposal.
Name the aim of removing misunderstanding.
Ask what language is for.
Read access to one another’s thought as a means of unity.
Connect a common medium with fellowship.
Keep the concise practical proposal.
shortened: Baha'u'llah has announced the necessity for a universal language which shall serve as a means of international communication and thus remove misunderstandings and difficulties.

order.why: Consider shared mental understanding.
Read language as one force of fellowship.
Hear the reported diagnosis of separation.
Place the historical account of estrangement in its source setting.
Read the Babel account as scriptural interpretation.
Let the reported travelers’ different words illustrate the problem.
Turn from aspiration to an appeal to parliaments.
Read the proposal for international consultation and selection.
Include rulers, ministers and education in the proposal.
Keep the House of Justice and common script in view.
shortened: From the beginning of time the light of unity hath shed its divine radiance upon the world, and the greatest means for the promotion of that unity is for the peoples of the world to understand one another's writing and speech. In former Epistles We have enjoined upon the Trustees of the House of Justice either to choose one language from among those now existing or to adopt a new one, and in like manner to select a common script, both of which should be taught in all the schools of the world. Thus will the earth be regarded as one country and one home.

order.why: Consider the role of bodies of learning.
Read the educational implementation through national bodies.
Attend to representation of peoples in the reported proposal.
Keep the concise instruction for schools.
Read the farther-reaching aspiration alongside the auxiliary model.
Examine linguistic exclusiveness in relation to world citizenship.
Locate language among the candles of unity.
shortened: The seventh candle is unity of language, i.e., the choice of a universal tongue in which all peoples will be instructed and converse.

order.why: Retain the brief enumeration.
shortened: Ninth, freedom of rights. Tenth, non-interference in political affairs. Eleventh, the establishment of a universal language. Twelfth, the Most Great Justice.

order.why: Set language within the teachings’ response to an age.
Read it beside equality, science, justice and freedom from prejudice.
Connect it with arbitration and economic well-being.
Keep the related connection with the economic question.
Read education and affiliation together.
Hear the appreciation of an auxiliary language’s possibilities.
Introduce Esperanto and gratitude for Zamenhof’s work.
shortened: Praise be to God, that Dr. Zamenhof has constructed the Esperanto language. It has all the potential qualities of universal adoption. All of us must be grateful and thankful to him for his noble effort for in this matter he has served his fellowmen well. He has constructed a language which will bestow divine benefits on all peoples.

order.why: Read encouragement together with continued improvement.
shortened: One of the great steps towards universal peace would be the establishment of a universal language. Baha'u'llah commands that the servants of humanity should meet together, and either choose a language which now exists, or form a new one.
If everybody could speak one language, how much more easy would it be to serve humanity!
Therefore appreciate 'Esperanto', for it is the beginning of the carrying out of one of the most important of the Laws of Baha'u'llah, and it must continue to be improved and perfected.

order.why: Retain the reported commitment to promote its study.
Notice the efforts of women learning the new language.
shortened: Praise be to God, it was evidence of the luminosity and spirituality of those handmaidens of the All-Merciful, that with perfect steadfastness and constancy you have undertaken to learn the new language and are occupied with thoughts and mention of the divine Kingdom.

order.why: Consider translation as a practical contribution.
Keep the particular counsel concerning Esperantists.
shortened: The matter of the Esperantists is more important than the League assembly. Jinab-i-Mr. Yazdani can sow a seed among them.

order.why: Preserve Hans Springer’s own statement of purpose.
Read the stated limits of Esperanto at that time.
Allow for revision or a more complete alternative.
Keep the historically situated advice about immediate language study.
Read the need for representative discussion and promotion.
Consider the reported council and proposed linguistic features.
shortened: "The love and effort put into Esperanto will not be lost," he answered, "but no one person can construct a Universal Language. It must be made by a Council representing all countries, and must contain words from different languages. It will be governed by the simplest rules, and there will be no exceptions; neither will there be gender, nor extra and silent letters. Everything indicated will have but one name.
In the schools of each nation the mother tongue will be taught, as well as the revised Universal Language."

order.why: Keep universal recognition as a condition of the anticipated results.
shortened: Forty years ago it was revealed in the Kitab-el-Akdas (Book of Laws) by the Blessed Perfection, that one language will be chosen as the means of universal communication. That language is now in the course of construction. If this new language which is being promulgated, shall be universally recognized, it will produce great results."

order.why: Read the expectation of scientific discussion.
Place the common medium beside other language learning.
shortened: 3.	The Religion of Unity must be nurtured with the aid of a unifying language and a unifying script; attention should also be paid to the learning of the most important languages of the world in addition to one's mother tongue.

order.why: Return to the reader’s responsibility to make an effort.
Retain the strongly expressed hope as an attributed report.
shortened: The greatest means of such a union is the universal language. It is most certain and indubitable that the universal language will completely wipe away all the differences from amongst mankind. This is clear and does not need any proof.

order.why: Join the hope for language with wider forms of unity.
shortened: This is the day of universal peace, of universal brotherhood, of a universal language and of the union of all religions.

order.why: Read the affectionate image of East and West meeting.
Keep the new language within the context of a reported dream.
Close with the imaginative invitation to a realm of mutual understanding.

questions: What kinds of human possibility are opened when people can understand one another directly?
How could a shared auxiliary language support both worldwide communication and the continued life of mother tongues?
What does the compilation suggest about who should participate in choosing and developing a common language?
How does the Pentecost account offer a different way to imagine understanding across linguistic diversity?
What can the Esperanto passages teach about encouraging an initiative while leaving room for revision and collective decision?
Which obstacles to peace might clearer communication help remove, and which would still require justice, goodwill, and changes in social relationships?

references.label: 1 · Acts 2:1–11 · Hearing across languages
references.note: At Pentecost, people from many places hear the disciples in their own languages. Read the account beside the aspiration for shared understanding in this compilation. Its multilingual hearing differs from the planned adoption of an auxiliary language, making the comparison a way to explore unity and diversity without treating the two accounts as the same proposal.
